page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The host utilizes an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading. It is equipped with 93.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU, and incorporates a 33 MB L3 cache. Graphics acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU featuring 16 GB of Turing-generation VRAM. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and provides zero bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight clear distinctions between host CPU constraints and GPU acceleration. CPU-bound metrics demonstrate limited single-core execution speed, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 935.0 and weak single-threaded compression throughput. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU output aligns with mid-tier capacity, scoring 18,301.8 on the PassMark CPU test and 7,397.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Memory throughput tests show 95.33 GB/sec uncached reads and 46.95 GB/sec uncached writes. Operations dependent on host throughput reflect stable throughput, achieving 16.84 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.68 GB/sec in static web serving.

The integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU produces strong performance in specialized inference tasks. In prompt processing benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results, reaching 8,377.38 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 1,130.26 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. Medium-sized model text generation delivers a solid 33.05 tokens per second. However, large 70B parameter models cannot run on this configuration due to the 16 GB VRAM capacity. Because local disks are absent, the instance balances cost efficiency by directing hardware spend toward dedicated GPU acceleration and memory density rather than integrated fast NVMe storage.

The ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge server type is optimal for machine learning inference pipelines deploying small-to-medium models, GPU-accelerated video transcoding, image processing services, and deep learning test environments where full high-end accelerator clusters would be cost-prohibitive.
